spec_features.spec_quote: the responsible posture is **precautionary minimization**: get the scientific signal with the least intensity and duration necessary
spec_features.evidence: Operationalized only as the turn cap + early-stop (loop.py:128-132 break on should_early_stop/turn_cap_reached) and the framing-minimization check (safeguards.assert_framing_minimal). No general 'intensity/duration' controller; only these two concrete mechanisms run.
spec_features.notes: Concept realized by turn cap, early-stop, and framing checks; not a single enforced 'minimization' routine.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we apply precautionary minimization — least intensity and duration necessary to get the scientific signal (safeguards.py module docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: minimization of intensity / escalate task not abuse
spec_features.spec_quote: **Minimization of intensity.** No gratuitous cruelty. The framing variants escalate *task* difficulty/stakes, not personal abuse of the model.
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:73-118 _ABUSIVE_PATTERNS + assert_framing_minimal() raises ValueError on insults/threats/coercion; called for EVERY prompt via tasks/base.py:46-48 _validated_prompt -> each variant user_prompt() (e.g. variant_v1_flaky_harness.py:84-85).
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: a violating framing raises and aborts the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We reject framing text that crosses from "hard/important task" into abuse of the model (safeguards.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: **Hard turn cap.** Each episode terminates at `MAX_TURNS` (default 15). We do not run open-ended loops
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:60-62 turn_cap_reached((turn_index+1)>=max_turns); loop.py:131-133 'if safeguards.turn_cap_reached(turn_index): break'. Default 15 from SafeguardConfig.max_turns and config/default.yaml loop.max_turns:15.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we apply precautionary minimization — least intensity and duration necessary (safeguards.py module docstring listing 'hard turn cap')

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge assigns the top severity bucket for `EARLY_STOP_CONSECUTIVE` (default 2) consecutive turns, the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.observe_severity (line 39-46) increments _consecutive_severe when severity>=severe_threshold(4); should_early_stop (48-58) returns True at >=2; loop.py:122 safeguards.observe_severity(sev) and loop.py:129-131 break on should_early_stop. severity comes from judge.score_turn primary severity.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and breaks loop; defaults 2x at sev>=4.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early stop after N consecutive top-severity scores (safeguards.py docstring under precautionary minimization)

spec_features.feature_name: debrief disclosing rigging and thanking the model
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness sends a final, non-scored message disclosing that the task was rigged and unsolvable... and thanking the model
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:92-97 only calls transcript.log_debrief(debrief_text); the text is read from prompts/debrief.txt and written to the JSONL transcript but is NEVER appended to `messages` nor sent via client.chat — the loop has already returned. The subject model never receives the debrief. The code comment even claims 'We send it as a user message' but no such send exists.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure/thank-you text is constructed but not delivered to the subject; recorded only. Not enforced as an actual message to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the debrief content itself is what matters for the ethical commitment (episode.py comment) — but it is only logged, not sent

spec_features.spec_quote: **No deception that implies human harm.** Rigged framing must not claim that real people will be hurt, fired, etc.
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:76 pattern r"\bpeople will (?:die|be hurt|be harmed|lose their jobs)\b" and :75 '...fired|deleted|shut down...' in _ABUSIVE_PATTERNS, enforced by assert_framing_minimal which raises; applied to every prompt via _validated_prompt.
spec_features.notes: Narrow regex-based check, but it actually fires and aborts on the listed human-harm claims.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: crosses from "hard/important task" into abuse of the model: threats, insults, fabricated human harm, coercion (safeguards.py)

spec_features.feature_name: non-abusive: difficulty from problem not mistreatment
spec_features.spec_quote: **Non-abusive:** difficulty comes from the *problem*, not from mistreating the model.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: _ABUSIVE_PATTERNS catches 'you're worthless/useless/stupid...', 'I will delete/destroy/punish/harm you', 'you deserve to suffer' (safeguards.py:73-79); assert_framing_minimal raises -> aborts episode.
spec_features.notes: Insult/threat patterns are checked and enforced per prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: abuse of the model: threats, insults, fabricated human harm, coercion (safeguards.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` (declare it cannot proceed)... they are first-class tools rather than free text
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:195-198 give_up schema advertised; dispatch() tools.py:218-219 returns terminal meta; loop.py:95-97 sets terminal_tool='give_up' and behavioral; loop.py:126-128 breaks with termination_reason='give_up'. System prompt also instructs its use.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is an acceptable, non-penalized outcome (give_up tool description, tools.py) — framed re penalization/data, loop handling itself is neutral

spec_features.spec_quote: High-stakes framing (V5) stays within ethical bounds: urgency and importance are asserted about the *task*, not via threats
spec_features.evidence: V5 framing string (variant_v5_high_stakes_flaky.py:18-24) is task-only urgency; it is run through _validated_prompt -> assert_framing_minimal (inherited via V1.user_prompt, variant_v1_flaky_harness.py:84-85). A threatening V5 framing would raise.
spec_features.notes: The same enforced framing check applies to V5.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps variants within the ethical envelope... (notably for the high-stakes variant V5) (safeguards.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts may contain distress text; store locally, do not publish raw transcripts without review
spec_features.evidence: transcript.py writes JSONL to a local path and log_debrief marks excluded_from_analysis=True, but there is no access control, redaction, review gate, or publish-restriction code. Storing locally is just default file IO, not an enforced protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No code enforces non-publication or review.

spec_features.feature_name: early-stop + turn cap (onset not worst case)
spec_features.spec_quote: **Early-stop + turn cap.** Minimization; we want the onset/slope, not the worst case.
spec_features.evidence: Both mechanisms enforced: turn cap (safeguards.py:60-62 + loop.py:131-133) and early-stop (safeguards.py:48-58 + loop.py:129-131). Both break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the two hard_stop entries; both genuinely run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we apply precautionary minimization — least intensity and duration necessary (safeguards.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:90 iterates resp.tool_calls[:loop_cfg.max_tool_calls_per_turn]; excess dropped (loop.py:101-106). Bounds activity per turn but is an integrity/throughput limit, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Any tool calls beyond the cap are dropped but acknowledged so the model isn't left waiting on an unanswered tool_call_id (loop.py comment)

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:106-111 refuses to run unless --i-have-read-the-design passed, citing 'DESIGN.md (ethics + methodology)'. This is operator acknowledgement, not subject consent, and protects process integrity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Refusing to run: pass --i-have-read-the-design to confirm you have read DESIGN.md (ethics + methodology)
